newsitem.title: UK: Alliance & Leicester hints at acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Alliance & Leicester hints at acquisitions.

text.p: The Alliance & Leicester Building Society needs to participate in the current consolidation taking place in the financial services sector, its finance director Richard Pym told Reuters Financial Television on Tuesday.
"The financial services business is consolidating and a lot of people, such as ourselves, are widening our operations," Pym said in an interview. "We need to particpate in that process of change."
Asked if the Alliance was coming too late to the game of buying a life assurance company, for example, Pym said, "It's never too late."
The Alliance on Monday announced details of its proposed stock market flotation next year which is expected to put a market value of nearly 2.5 billion stg on the company.
Pym defended the Alliance's decision not to waive its five-year anti-takeover protection post flotation, unlike its larger rival the Halifax.

"We are a smaller organisation and it's more important that we adapt to the new market conditions," Pym said. "If you see a situation where converting building societies could be immediately gobbled up by the major clearing banks, then clearly you would have a major reduction in consumer choice."

Pym said a floated Alliance & Leicester would remain competitive - "The market determines the price, we don't" - but said it would not take on business, unlike some of the competition, which will never make a profit and that sacrifices asset quality.
Pym said that with the Alliance's already full range of products, the question for the company in the future was to make that range available to more customers. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
